items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the advisory council and the domestic violence fatality review team
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5394

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to
the advisory council and the domestic violence fatality review team

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would add new members to the Office for the Prevention of
Domestic Violence's (OPDV) Advisory Council and the Domestic Violence
Fatality Review team.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 would amend subdivision four of section- 575 of the
Executive Law to add the Superintendent of the Division of State
Police as an ex-officio member of the Advisory Council.

Section 2 would amend subdivision ten of section 575 of the Executive
Law to add the Office of Victim Services to the Domestic Violence
Fatality Review team.

Section 3 would make it effective immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

OPDV's Advisory Council was established to make recommendations on
domestic violence-related issues and effective strategies for the
prevention of domestic violence, to assist in the development of
policies for effective intervention, public education and advocacy,
and to facilitate and assure communication and coordination of efforts
among state agencies and between state, federal and local levels of
government. Law enforcement must be an essential part of coordinating
and responding effectively to domestic violence. In addition to
policing duties statewide, the New York State Police are the primary,
or only, law enforcement presence in a significant portion of the
state.

The Domestic Violence Fatality Review team was created in 2012 to
analyze domestic violence-related deaths or near deaths of
individuals, examine trends and patterns of domestic violence-related
fatalities in New York state, educate the public, service providers,
and policymakers about domestic violence fatalities and strategies for
intervention and prevention, and recommend policies and services to
reduce domestic violence fatalities. The Office of Victim Services
(OVS) plays a vital role in funding services for crime victims, and
providing financial compensation to victims. Since victim interface
with local service networks is an issue that the fatality review team
examines, OVS would gain important insight into victim needs through
participation in case reviews, and offer valuable information to the
team.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The bill would take effect immediately.
